note: Observed MMT-9 light curves (Karpov et al. 2016, mmt.favor2.info) of three Starlink passes, collected for tools/video. Samples: [utc, apparent Clear mag, range_km (MMT, from its TLE), phase_deg (MMT), channel, standard mag]. V = Clear - 0.09 (Mallama 2021). TLEs recovered from CelesTrak snapshots in the Wayback Machine; tle_time_offset_s fitted to MMT's range column.

source.citation: A. Mallama 2021, 'Starlink Satellite Brightness -- Characterized From 100,000 Visible Light Magnitudes', arXiv:2111.09735, Section 8, Figure 13 ('Flaring of Starlink-1538 recorded on 2021 May 2') - the published figure is this MMT track (the only STARLINK-1538 track that night); data from Karpov et al. 2016, 'Massive photometry of low-altitude artificial satellites on Mini-Mega-TORTORA', RMxAC 48, 112; data: MMT-9 satellite database http://mmt.favor2.info/satellites

passes.version: Starlink VisorSat (launch 2020-08-07, 2020-055 = the first all-VisorSat launch; the repo's mallama2021_visorsat.json calls it L9)

observer.source: mmt.favor2.info/satellites page text: 41d25m53.3s E, 43d38m59.5s N, 2030 m

passes.magnitude_system: MMT-9 'Clear' (unfiltered white light) magnitudes calibrated to Johnson V with field stars; Karpov: Clear ~ V + 0.15(B-V), i.e. V = Clear - 0.09 for solar colour (Mallama 2021 arXiv:2111.09735 App. A). The 'Mag' column is the apparent magnitude (not range/phase normalised); Mallama 2021 describes these as apparent magnitudes corrected for atmospheric extinction only - MMT does not document this per column, treat as uncertain. Per-point scatter ~0.1-0.2 mag (0.18 rms between simultaneous channels).
passes.cadence: ~10 Hz (0.1 s frames) per channel, sometimes 0.2-0.5 s; each point is one frame on one of 9 channels (71 mm f/1.2 lenses, sCMOS); gaps where the satellite crosses between channel fields
passes.flare: Main flare peak 2021-05-02 23:53:50.9 UTC: baseline ~6.9 -> 5.54 (single frame; 1-s median 5.6), ~1.3-1.4 mag, FWHM ~1.5 s (23:53:50.2-23:53:52.0). A weak one-frame blip at ~23:53:20.5 (6.96 vs ~7.35). Data gap 23:53:37.1-23:53:45.4 (channel 3 -> 1). Underlying trend brightens from ~7.4 to ~6.85 as range falls 797 -> 612 km at nearly constant phase 81.5-83.3 deg.
passes.tle_source: CelesTrak starlink.txt (18 SDS GP), Wayback Machine snapshot 20210420224510 (tle_wayback/celestrak_starlink_20210420224510.txt)

tle_alternatives.source: CelesTrak starlink.txt (18 SDS GP), Wayback Machine snapshot 20210420224510 (tle_wayback/celestrak_starlink_20210420224510.txt)
CelesTrak SupGP (SpaceX-ephemeris-derived) supplemental/starlink.txt, Wayback snapshot 20210429223717. Classification 'C', non-standard checksum; python sgp4 parses it.

passes.tle_note: No public TLE within 3 days of the pass was found (Space-Track, login required, would have the element set MMT used, epoch ~2021-05-01). MMT identified the track with a TLE of age 1.4 d and reports a residual of -240+-39 arcsec along-track (~0.8 km, ~0.1 s) and -102+-10 arcsec cross-track (~0.35 km), so the MMT range_km column is a good reference: evaluate the TLE at t_obs + fit_time_offset_s. Offsets were fitted with SGP4 against the MMT range column. The bracketing TLEs disagree by -3.0 s / +3.25 s without the shift (~20-25 km along track, i.e. ~2 deg on the sky), so the shift matters. Cross-track error after the shift is unknown (< ~1-2 km).
uncertain: MMT range_km / phase_deg are computed by MMT from its TLE, not measured
Per-frame scatter 0.1-0.2 mag; smooth with a ~1 s median before comparing
Flare times depend on attitude details (array angle, roll) the simulator models generically
Penumbra flag is 0 for every sample (fully sunlit)

passes.tle_note: Nearest public TLE found is 16.7 days AFTER the pass; it matches the MMT range only with a -5.0 s shift. The 2020-12-04 TLE (Wayback 20201205) does not fit at all (>60 s; a manoeuvre in between). Two simultaneous channels (2 and 7) give 15 duplicate time stamps. MMT's own TLE (age 1.5 d) had a residual of -3417+-160 arcsec along track (~10 km) for a different track of this series, so V1.0 orbits of that period were maneuvering; weakest orbit of the three.
